transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood CSM), Diego (Redwood SE), Dr. Amanda Chen (SLH), Jason Holt (SLH), Priya Ramesh (SLH)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated): Kickoff to align timeline, pilot, security controls; Redwood to provision test VPC and run SE deep-dive next week.

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to kick off with SilverLake. quick intros, i'll run through agenda then hand off to diego for tech items.
[00:00:12] Amanda: Hi, Amanda here, head of data at SilverLake. excited to get this started.
[00:00:16] Jason: Jason, platform lead, i'll own infra and the pilot execution.
[00:00:19] Priya: Priya from security, i'll be covering compliance questions.
[00:00:22] Maya: Great. Ethan?
[00:00:24] Ethan: Ethan, CSM - i'll run project coordination and onboarding tasks.
[00:00:27] Diego: Diego, SE, i'll do the deep-dive and help with network/provisioning.
[00:00:32] Maya: Agenda: 1) timeline and success criteria for pilot, 2) infra options - hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC, 3) security and compliance Qs, 4) next steps. quick check, any additions?
[00:00:45] Jason: sounds good. maybe we add data residency and audit log retention.
[00:00:49] Maya: Yep we'll cover that.

[00:02:05] Maya: To set context, our recommended flow for regulated customers is private VPC deployment with Redwood's private control plane and customer-managed networking. gives you isolation and key management integration.
[00:02:21] Amanda: We have to be careful with PHI touching third-party systems. our priority is data residency and key control.
[00:02:28] Maya: Understood. we support KMS integrations and HSM for key wrapping, and we can configure tokenization or redaction at ingestion. we'll share the docs.
[00:03:05] Priya: Are you SOC2 Type II covered for the private deploy? we need audit logs and evidence for audits.
[00:03:12] Diego: Yes, Redwood's platform has SOC2 controls for hosted and we have an enterprise package for private that includes audit log exports; note that some log collectors are customer-managed in VPC. we'll send the SOC2 pack and the compliance matrix.
[00:03:34] Priya: also need SSO/SAML and RBAC integration details.
[00:03:38] Ethan: We have an SSO guide, will attach it to the welcome packet.

[00:05:10] Diego: on infra: for pilot we usually recommend a small dedicated pool or a private VPC on a single region. it's more predictable for latency. hosted is simplest, but for PHI many customers choose private.
[00:05:24] Jason: Latency is a concern for our clinician-facing features - sub 200ms token latency ideally. can Redwood meet that in private?
[00:05:33] Diego: depends on model and quantization; with dedicated GPUs and optimized runtime we can get low latency. we'll propose a config: 1 node gpus with int8 quantization and prefix caching; we'll run benchmarks during pilot.
[00:06:00] Amanda: good. can you explain caching briefly? i keep seeing KV cash in other docs :)
[00:06:06] Diego: ha, KV cache, yes - we do prefix / KV cache so repeated context doesn't re-compute, helps token cost and latency. our runtime also does smart batching but for low-latency we'll tune batch windows.

[00:08:15] Maya: Pilot scope suggestion: 6 weeks, 2 workloads: 1) clinician note summarization pipeline (batch), 2) real-time triage assistant in web UI (latency-critical). success metrics: latency under 200ms for realtime, accuracy defined by F1 > .85 on dev prompts, and cost target per 1k requests.
[00:08:37] Jason: we can provide sample prompts and historic examples.
[00:08:41] Amanda: plus we need to validate redaction and retention - e.g., which fields must be dropped.
[00:08:46] Priya: retention policy: logs must be retained for 12 months and audit trail exportable. does Redwood support SIEM export?
[00:08:54] Diego: yes, we can stream audit logs to customer S3 or syslog; for private deployments it's customer-managed.

[00:12:10] Maya: On roles: we'll set up RBAC; we recommend least privilege for SE and app tokens per environment.
[00:12:20] Priya: also need encryption at rest and in transit - i assume TLS for transit and KMS for rest?
[00:12:26] Diego: correct, TLS in transit, KMS integration for key management; you can bring your own key or use managed.

[00:15:02] Maya: Pricing for pilot - for private we typically do a short reserved commit or trial credits. i'll follow up with pricing sheet; goal is not to block pilot.
[00:15:15] Jason: good, want to avoid long procurement before pilot.

[00:18:30] Amanda: timeline constraints - our compliance board meets on Oct 5th, so if we can show pilot results before then that's ideal.
[00:18:38] Ethan: target to have pilot started by 2027-09-27, run through early Oct so results can be compiled.

[00:21:50] Diego: action on tech side: we'll need network peering details, egress rules, and firewall ports. typically we ask for a jump host and a customer infra contact.
[00:21:58] Jason: i'll be the infra contact, i'll share network team details.

[00:25:10] Priya: security questionnaire - we have a standard vendor questionnaire, can Redwood complete it?
[00:25:16] Maya: yes we can complete the questionnaire; we'll also share our compliance pack.

[00:28:40] Diego: for evaluation we propose these benchmarks: throughput for batch summary (docs per minute), p99 latency for realtime, and token cost estimate. we'll run a baseline on our recommended model family - we can test a small open model and also a Redwood-curated variant.
[00:29:05] Amanda: are there model choices that are better for PHI?
[00:29:10] Diego: model choice is more about fine-tuning and quantization; we can use a private fine-tuned model if needed. we'll discuss model onboarding separately.

[00:33:02] Maya: questions from legal/procurement?
[00:33:06] Priya: just terms around data processing addendum and breach notification timelines.
[00:33:12] Maya: standard DPA included in enterprise package, breach notif within 72 hours for incidents; we'll share legal contacts and template.

[00:36:20] Ethan: recap of next week: diego will run deep-dive and network workshop; maya will send welcome packet and pricing; ethan will provision test env once we get network details.
[00:36:33] Jason: plan to share prompts and dataset by 2027-09-21.
[00:36:38] Amanda: and we'll loop in compliance folks for the Oct 5 checkpoint.

[00:40:00] Maya: any final Qs?
[00:40:03] Priya: just curious about competitor differences, you mentioned Anthropic and others - what's the main difference for us?
[00:40:10] Diego: main diff is that Redwood focuses on production runtime and deterministic economics - scheduling, batching, and provable latency SLOs; competitors may offer models but not same integration for private VPC and observability.
[00:41:02] Amanda: ok that helps.

[00:50:12] Maya: i'll summarize with actions and send notes. thanks everyone.
[00:50:20] Ethan: thanks all, will book the deep-dive for 2027-09-22 14:00 UTC (tentative).
[00:50:26] Jason: thanks.
[00:50:30] Amanda: thanks.
[00:50:33] Priya: bye.

[00:54:00] (call ends)
